_meta.note: Grading bands for SHIPPED scripts. The live writer (backend/dvsu_script_v2.py) uses the same 95-120 target but a tighter 80-150 generation ceiling: only 6 of 373 gold paragraphs exceed 150 and none exceed 170, so 170 stays the grading hard_max here while 150 is the point past which a generated draft is repaired rather than accepted.

paragraph_word_count.empirical_note: Pooled across all 14 gold scripts (373 paragraphs): median 107, p10 84, p90 129. 90/373 (24%) fall under 95 and 66/373 (18%) run over 120 - the written 'never less, never more' is aspirational, not what ships. Outside target band is a warning, not a rejection; only outside the hard band is a violation.

paragraph_count_per_video.doc_claim: 24-30 paragraphs. Below 15 too short. Above 32 retention drops (split into Part 1/2).
paragraph_count_per_video.empirical_note: Gold script paragraph counts range 23-33; several run slightly under 24 or over 30 and are still shipped, so under/over target is a warning, not a rejection. Only under the 15 floor or over 32 is a violation.

acts_per_video.doc_claim: 4-7 acts per video, each summarizable in one sentence.
acts_per_video.note: None of the 14 gold scripts carry act headers in the narration body (act structure is thematic, not marked - see DvsU_Script_Writing_System.md's 'ACTS' section and QL-47's ban on act labels in the voiceover file). This cannot be graded from script_text alone; check() accepts an optional act_count to validate this rule when the outline stage supplies it, and otherwise reports it as 'not_checked'.

name_openers.pattern_doc: Bare 'The [Maker] [Designation/Name] ...' opener, e.g. 'The Boeing XB-15 first flew...'
name_openers.doc_claim: Maximum 4-5 paragraphs out of 30 may open with the unit's name.
name_openers.empirical_note: Per-script bare-name-opener share across the 14 gold fixtures ranges 0% to 83% (bomber script 83%, most-hated-helicopters 68%, most scripts 0-26%). The written 4-5-of-30 ceiling (~17%) is violated by several shipped scripts, most dramatically the strategic-bomber script, which opens almost every paragraph with the machine's name. This is an open tension between the written standard and shipped practice (same shape as storyengine/notes/dvsu-quality-law.md's QL-7, which found a pooled ~57% share and set severity to 'warn', not 'hard-gate'). check() warns above warn_share and separately reports the doc's stricter ideal as guidance; it does not hard-reject on this rule.

forbidden_patterns.note: Written standard bans these outright, but 4 of the 14 gold scripts use them 11 times (mostly 'revolutionary design/concept', including one deliberate negation - 'Caldwell wasn't revolutionary. It was practical.' - that directly serves the anti-hype thesis rather than violating it). Downgraded to warning rather than hard-gate, matching dvsu-quality-law.md's QL-12 pattern of warning on an unanchored superlative rather than banning the word outright.

ending_rule.doc_claim: The video ends on the final unit. No separate conclusion paragraph.
ending_rule.check: forbidden_patterns' conclusion_language group is re-checked against the final paragraph specifically, since a summary close is the one forbidden pattern most likely to appear only at the very end.
